access_notes: Read 2026-10-30 (T-3250) through a fetch that returned the essay in summary and short quoted fragments, never a whole paragraph; cited only for what those fragments say.
note: Fragments read: Henrietta Greenebaum Frank (1608) and Ella Walker (1720) 'worked steadily for quality nursing education at the Illinois Training School for Nurses'; Jane Grahame Jones (1834) 'fought for woman suffrage.' The essay also says the residents supported the Visiting Nurses Association and helped found the Art Institute, and that after the 1890s many leading families died or moved to suburbs such as Lake Forest. Re-read 2026-11-07 for the street's decline: in 1910 wreckers destroyed the mansion at 1720, the first of many Prairie Avenue homes to be torn down; residences increasingly gave way to offices, warehouses and factories; by 1930 the elite world of Prairie Avenue had all but disappeared.
what_it_supplies: Henrietta Greenebaum Frank of 1608 and Ella Walker of 1720 working for nursing education at the Illinois Training School for Nurses
Jane Grahame Jones of 1834 fighting for woman suffrage
the 1910 loss of 1720 Prairie as the street's first teardown, and the turn from homes to offices, warehouses and factories
